question: Should `openclaw/plugin-sdk/reply-payload` expose a generic `tool-progress` kind and predicate as a permanent public contract distinct from `ReplyPayload.isStatusNotice`?
rationale: The distinction is technically defensible because `isStatusNotice` is broader and affects core reply behavior, but adding public plugin API surface is a compatibility and ownership decision that requires maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve narrow progress contract
options.body: Keep the generic kind and predicate, require exact-head Slack lifecycle proof, and treat only explicitly typed disposable summaries as suppressible.

options.title: Reuse broad status flag
options.body: Refactor the producer and Slack consumer to `isStatusNotice`, accepting that it also represents visible lifecycle notices and changes core threading and coalescing semantics.

options.title: Keep the signal private
options.body: Avoid public SDK expansion through a plugin-local or existing generic seam, which may require a broader ownership refactor between the Codex and Slack plugins.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow progress contract
recommendation.body: Keep the generic kind and predicate, require exact-head Slack lifecycle proof, and treat only explicitly typed disposable summaries as suppressible.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent current-main work owns both the Slack reply path and the existing reply-payload progress/status contracts needed to decide the permanent API boundary.
